title: Network & Wi-Fi
blurb: No internet, slow or dropping Wi-Fi, can't see other computers.

remedies.title: No internet after removing a VPN or security app
remedies.why: VPN and security apps add network filters; a messy uninstall can leave them behind.

steps.text: Restart the computer first.
Reset the network stack (removes leftover filters; restart needed).
Remove leftover VPN profiles and network extensions.
Check the proxy settings are clear.

remedies.title: Phone has internet but the computer doesn't (same Wi-Fi)
symptoms: other devices work but not pc
remedies.why: The problem is on this computer: its network settings, a VPN/proxy, security software or its Wi-Fi driver.

steps.text: Run the Network doctor.
Forget the network and rejoin.
Turn off VPN, proxy and third-party firewall for a test.
Clear the address cache, then reset the network if needed.

remedies.title: Internet is down for every device at home or in the office
remedies.why: The router, modem or the provider's line is down.

steps.text: Look at the router/modem lights; a red or off "Internet" light means the line.
Restart the modem and router: unplug 30 seconds, plug the modem in first, wait 2 minutes, then the router.
Check the provider's outage page on mobile data.
Use a phone hotspot meanwhile.

remedies.escalate: In the office, tell IT; at home, call your provider with the router lights' state.

remedies.title: Lag in calls and games (high ping), even though speed is fine
remedies.why: Latency and packet loss matter more than speed for calls and games; Wi-Fi and busy uploads cause spikes.

steps.text: Use a cable, or the 5 GHz network near the router.
Pause big uploads (cloud backup, photo sync) during calls.
Routers with QoS / "Smart Queue" settings can keep calls smooth.

remedies.title: Share my laptop's internet with another device
remedies.why: The computer can act as a Wi-Fi hotspot.

steps.text: Settings › Network & internet › Mobile hotspot.
System Settings › General › Sharing › Internet Sharing.

remedies.escalate: Work networks often forbid sharing; ask IT.

remedies.title: Some sites fail or are slow, others fine (possible IPv6 trouble)
remedies.why: A broken IPv6 setup at the router or provider makes some sites stall before falling back.

steps.text: Restart the router; check for a firmware update.
As a test, turn off IPv6 on the adapter (Network Connections › Wi-Fi › Properties › untick IPv6); turn it back on afterwards.
Report it to the provider if it fixes things.

remedies.escalate: Leave IPv6 settings to IT on work devices.

remedies.title: See which devices are on my Wi-Fi
remedies.why: The router lists connected devices; unknown ones may mean someone has your password.

steps.text: Open the router's app or admin page › Connected devices.
If you see devices you don't know, change the Wi-Fi password (all devices rejoin).

remedies.title: No internet after waking from sleep
remedies.why: The Wi-Fi adapter doesn't wake properly, often due to power saving.

steps.text: Turn Wi-Fi off and on.
Stop power saving on the adapter: Device Manager › Network adapters › Wi-Fi › Power Management.
Update the Wi-Fi driver.
Update macOS; restart if it keeps happening.
